author: Memphis Standard
title: Memphis Tigers softball season ends with loss to UTSA in conference opener
text:
The University of Memphis softball team concluded its season on May 6 with an 8-6 loss to the University of Texas at San Antonio in the opening round of the American Conference Championships at Max R. Joyner Stadium.
The outcome brings an end to Memphis’ campaign, which saw them finish with a record of 18-39. The Tigers scored three runs in both the first and seventh innings, but eight runs by UTSA between those frames led to their elimination from the tournament.
According to the team, “The opening round game puts Memphis at 57 games played, tied for the fourth-most in a season.” The Tigers achieved a .283 batting average this year, marking it as the fourth-highest single-season total for the program (excluding shortened seasons). Their slugging percentage reached .445, setting a new single-season program record for teams with more than 1,000 at-bats. Additionally, Memphis posted a .370 on-base percentage and collected 397 hits—both among their best historical performances.
Several players reached notable milestones during this final game and throughout the season. One player finished her collegiate career as Memphis’ doubles leader for the year and tied for fourth-most doubles in a single season. Another Tiger became only the second since 2022 to achieve a 60-hit season and set new marks for multi-hit games and total bases. Other highlights include individual records in sacrifice hits, stolen bases, defensive assists, and slugging percentages across various positions on the roster.
Looking forward, fans are encouraged to follow updates about Memphis Tigers Softball through official channels online and on social media platforms.
